solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Irish writer's college

definitions.meaning: belonging to Oliver Goldsmith, the Irish author of The Vicar of Wakefield
a college of the University of London in New Cross

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one spelling: the possessive of the Irish author's surname and the London college's name.

clue.text: When bookmakers get worried they may change for the better

definitions.text: When bookmakers get worried they may change for the better

parts.words: When bookmakers get worried they may change for the better
parts.note: a nervous bookie shortens or lengthens the prices offered on a horse, so the betting terms shift in the punter's favour

explanation.definitionFit: Betting prices are what bookmakers alter when worried about liabilities, and a change can favour the gambler.

clue.text: Boy upset half the girls in US city

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word for boy is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a boy is a lad

indicators.note: half of the six-letter word for girls is kept, its first three letters

parts.note: girls are lasses

explanation.surface: A lad upsets several girls in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LAD into DAL; 'half' keeps LAS from LASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas is a large city in Texas, United States.

clue.text: Deceive a thousand ladies naughtily

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: behaving naughtily suggests the letters of ladies misbehave and rearrange

explanation.surface: A thousand misbehaving ladies trick someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughtily' rearranges LADIES into ISLEAD, after M.
explanation.definitionFit: To deceive someone is to lead them astray, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Those people taking subject, not finishing

indicators.note: not finishing means the final letter of the word for subject is dropped

parts.note: a subject or topic is a theme

explanation.surface: Some people take up a subject but never complete it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing' drops the last E of THEME.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun them refers to those people already mentioned.

clue.text: Became comfortable in beast's home, having got shown the way

parts.note: a sett is a badger's burrow
to have shown the way is to have led

explanation.surface: An animal grew comfortable in its lair once it had been guided there.
explanation.walkthrough: A sett is the British name for a badger's underground home.
explanation.definitionFit: To have settled is to have become comfortable and established somewhere.

clue.text: Neat, normal, frightfully pretty

indicators.note: frightfully suggests the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something tidy and ordinary is described as dreadfully attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightfully' looks like an intensifier for pretty but rearranges NEAT and NORMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental means decorative or attractive, close in sense to pretty.

clue.text: Cricket? One of the XI is a sort of warden

parts.note: cricket is a game
the wicket-keeper is one of a cricket team's eleven players

explanation.surface: A question about cricket and its eleven players leads to a kind of guardian.
explanation.walkthrough: XI is eleven, the size of a cricket team, whose wicket-keeper is often called the keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamekeeper guards game birds and animals on an estate, a kind of warden.

clue.text: Sailor cautious — whale lurking!

indicators.note: lurking means the letters lie concealed within the words sailor cautious

explanation.surface: A careful seaman watches out because a whale is nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca, or killer whale, is the largest member of the dolphin family.

clue.text: Youth's progress upwards when receiving state aid

indicators.note: receiving means the word for progress upwards takes in the other piece

parts.note: an ascent is a climb, progress upwards
the dole is state unemployment benefit in Britain

explanation.surface: A young person climbs the ladder while living on benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts DOLE inside ASCENT after its A; the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a teenager, someone in adolescence.

clue.text: Possible result of road rage when one's stuck in traffic

indicators.note: stuck in means the letter for one is lodged inside the word for traffic

parts.note: traffic in goods is trade
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Drivers stuck in a jam lose their tempers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' looks like cars on a road but here means trade, the dealing in goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A furious driver may launch into a long angry speech, a rant.

clue.text: Conference centre being idiotic, cease going back

indicators.note: going back means the whole run of both pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: idiotic can mean mad
to cease is to stop

explanation.surface: A venue for meetings is behaving stupidly and refusing to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns MADSTOP into POTSDAM; the 1945 Allied conference was held there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potsdam Conference of 1945 settled post-war Germany, so the town is a famous conference site.

clue.text: Pair holding English translation to be a misrepresentation

indicators.note: holding means the abbreviation for pair wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a translation is a version of a text

explanation.surface: A couple of translators produce a distorted English rendering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts E and VERSION between P and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A perversion of the truth is a distortion, a misrepresentation.

clue.text: Women fix heaters all over the shop

indicators.note: all over the shop means in disarray, so the letters are scattered and reordered

explanation.surface: Some women repair heating appliances throughout a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the shop' (British for chaotic) rearranges FIX and HEATERS.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned phrase for women collectively, now often thought patronising.

clue.text: Mum, right friend to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with says the word for friend comes first, before the other letter

parts.note: a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A mother is the right friend to start with.
explanation.definitionFit: Mater is Latin for mother, used in old-fashioned British slang for one's mum.

clue.text: Think British priest will be attracted to temptress

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel
Eve tempted Adam with the apple

explanation.surface: Imagine a British clergyman falling for a seductive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To believe something is to think it true.

clue.text: Operatic composer in film business to start with

indicators.note: to start with places the word for business ahead of the film

parts.note: biz is informal for business, as in showbiz
E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film

explanation.surface: A composer of operas makes his start in the film industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Bizet was the French composer of the opera Carmen.

clue.text: Old king's daughter, singer making return

indicators.note: making return means the word for singer is read backwards

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female singer

explanation.surface: A former monarch's daughter, a singer, comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making return' turns DIVA into AVID.
explanation.definitionFit: David was the biblical king of Israel, an ancient monarch.

clue.text: Bird runs ahead with wings clipped

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: with wings clipped means the first and last letters of ahead are cut off

explanation.surface: A bird with clipped wings runs on in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with wings clipped' takes the outer letters off AHEAD, leaving HEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird.

clue.text: Course of action unreasonable, heartless

indicators.note: heartless means one of the central letters of the word for unreasonable is removed

parts.note: a steep price is unreasonable

explanation.surface: An unreasonable and cruel plan of action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops one middle E from STEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a measure taken, a course of action.

clue.text: Female hugging the Parisian is an exceptional beauty

indicators.note: hugging means the word for female wraps round the French article

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A woman embraces a Frenchman who is remarkably good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hugging' puts LE inside HEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Helen of Troy is the byword for supreme beauty.

clue.text: Place of residence that's sumptuous — in short, grand

parts.note: a home is where one lives

indicators.note: in short means the word for sumptuous is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: sumptuous means rich

explanation.surface: A lavish house described as, briefly, magnificent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' cuts RICH to RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Homeric means on an epic scale, grand like Homer's poems.

clue.text: Mad person's shell?

parts.note: read as the hard covering of a kernel, the husk round a walnut, though the phrase means a lunatic

explanation.definitionFit: A crazy person is colloquially called this, while literally it could be the hard casing of a kernel.

clue.text: Permanently resting performer seen as demanding person

parts.note: ex means former; resting is theatre slang for out of work
an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: A retired actor is regarded as hard to please.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resting' is the stage euphemism for an actor between jobs; permanently resting makes him a former actor.
explanation.definitionFit: An exactor is one who exacts, demanding payment or obedience.

clue.text: Butler deployed around back of room to offer a glass

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go round the other letter
deployed suggests the letters of butler are set out in new positions
back of means the final letter of room is taken

explanation.surface: A butler moving around the back of the room offers drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges BUTLER to TUBLER; 'around' puts M (from 'back of room') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler is a flat-bottomed drinking glass.

clue.text: Coloured bead is broken

indicators.note: broken means the letters of bead is are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A tinted bead turns out to be cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coloured' looks like a description of the bead but means prejudiced.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured judgement is distorted by prejudice, so it is biased.

clue.text: Awkward situation when academic room's put next to a gym

parts.note: SCR is the senior common room of a British college
PE, physical education, is gym class

explanation.surface: Trouble arises when a staff lounge sits beside a gymnasium.
explanation.walkthrough: SCR is the senior common room, the staff room at a British university.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is a tight spot, an awkward predicament.

clue.text: Silk handkerchief shows an Eastern inn

indicators.note: shows means the letters are on display within the words silk handkerchief

explanation.surface: A silk hanky is on display at an Oriental hostelry.
explanation.definitionFit: A khan is a caravanserai, an inn for travellers in Asia.

clue.text: Remarkable person one on the way out? No good

indicators.note: no good means the G abbreviation for good is removed

parts.note: a goner is someone about to die or be dismissed

explanation.surface: An outstanding person is leaving and is no use any more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No good' removes G from GONER.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is British slang for an exceptional person or thing.

clue.text: Try once more to get Carol practising

parts.note: to rehear a case is to try it again in court
to carol is to sing

explanation.surface: Have another go so Carol can practise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the legal sense, hearing a case; 'Carol' looks like a name but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehearsing is practising before a performance.

clue.text: Old stars getting a spread at the meal table

parts.note: Leo is a constellation

explanation.surface: Ageing celebrities sit down to a feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleo is short for oleomargarine, margarine spread on bread.

clue.text: Study bids to get work from competitors

parts.note: to con is to study carefully
tenders are formal bids for work

explanation.surface: Rivals examine bids to win contracts.
explanation.definitionFit: Contenders are rivals in a competition.
